paras: The lynching of Jake Evans was the hanging of a Black man by a mob at Auburn, Alabama, in the summer of 1885, after he was arrested on an accusation of assaulting a white woman. According to the only report found, the mob overpowered the officers who held him and hanged him to a tree. The event is known from a single wire paragraph that ran in two Dakota weeklies between August and September 1885.

Evans, described as "a negro," was said to have "brutally assaulted a white woman" at Auburn; the woman was not named, and the item gave no date or details of the alleged assault. He was arrested, but a mob then "overpowered the officers" and hanged him to a tree. The report gave no names of mob members, no number, and no date for the hanging, which took place on or before August 12, when the earliest printing found appeared.
No report of an inquest, of arrests of mob members, or of any official response was found in the coverage.

The Union County Courier of Elk Point, Dakota Territory, printed the paragraph on August 12, 1885, in an "Items From the South" column alongside a coal discovery in Texas and a Treasury defalcation in New Orleans. The same paper ran it again on August 26 and September 30, and the Turner County Herald of Hurley, Dakota Territory, carried it on September 3, 10 and 24, each time in the same words. The item stated the accusation as fact and reported the hanging without comment.
No account from an Alabama paper and no Black-press report of the lynching was found.

reader.title: Lynching of Jake Evans
bases: The only report says a mob overpowered the officers holding Jake Evans after his arrest and hanged him to a tree (A2).

A2 reports that a 'mob' took Evans from officers by force and hanged him, after he was accused of assaulting a white woman; the number in the mob is not given, but a mob that overpowered the officers implies more than two people. The account rests on a single wire paragraph.
All six printings (A2, A3, A4, A6, A7, A8) carry one identical wire paragraph in two Dakota papers; no independent, local or Black-press report was found.
